I. Core Vision:
A Dual-Environment Narrative Universe Development System:
Development Application: A flexible and robust environment to create, organize, test, and evolve complex universes.
Performance Application: A powerful live performance platform for bringing the universes to life through real-time audio and video manipulation.

Emphasis on Structure, Flexibility & Openness: Both applications must be adaptable and designed to grow, while also retaining a coherent and clear core structure.
Human-AI Collaboration: Both environments must prioritize a creative relationship with AI, and an acknowledgement that human input and intention is at the core of all creative processes, rather than having AI act as a control.
Ethical Grounding: Both environments must adhere to a strong set of ethical principles, and must respect diverse contexts, while promoting a positive impact.
II. Core Goals:
Modular Design: To build individual, standalone, but integrated systems.
 Format as Foundation: Use a custom markdown format to store data in a clear, portable and extensible format.
Actionable Results: To ensure every component performs verifiable functions, and delivers tangible results.
Step-by-Step Development: To use an iterative and clear approach to development.
Iterative Refinement: To enable continuous learning and improvement via user feedback and data-driven insights.
III. Key Components (Dual Application):
A. Narrative Universe Development Environment (Drafting Application):
Multiverse Manager:
Creates, loads, saves, manages, synthesizes and allows switching between universes.

Universe Architect:
Defines the core themes, rules, and archetypes for a given universe, including its cosmologies and metaphysical laws.

Story Composer:
Creates and edits text, scene descriptions, character profiles, or dialogue.
Provides tools for adhering to established structural and thematic rulesets.

Integrates with a flexible prompting system.
Sensory Designer:
Defines and manages visual, audio, and other sensory styles for different parts of a universe, and outputs clear and easy to use data for other systems.
**Character Designer:** Creates character profiles that are designed for both use in the drafting environment and the performance application.
*    **Prompt Management System:** Manages, tests and stores prompts across multiple AI models and use cases.
*   **Feedback & Testing System:** Analyzes and validates outputs from other modules, testing for ethical, narrative, or functional gaps.
Synthesis Engine: Merges multiple universe’s parameters, stories, or other components into new hybrid creations.
B. Live Performance Environment (Performance Application):
Live Input/Output System: A core system to capture real time information and send it to the different components.

Performance Director: An orchestration module to organize playback, AI-generation, and response to user interactions.
* TouchDesigner Integration: For live visual manipulation, generative content, and data output.
VST & Max for Live Integration: For dynamic audio processing and effects.

Real Time Control System: A user interface that prioritizes accessibility and fast adjustments in a live performance setting
Dynamic Synthesis: Enables mixing of components from multiple universes in real time.
IV. Data Flow & Workflow:
Universe Management (Multiverse Manager): Choose or create a new universe.
Framework Definition (Universe Architect): Define overarching themes, metaphysical rules, and core settings. Also define Archetypes which will be used as a structural guide for your story and for character design.
Narrative Structure Design (Story Composer): Use a text editor, and test your work with an AI powered system to ensure it meets certain structural, ethical, or thematic guidelines. Generate text or prompts for specific scenes, dialogues, or descriptions of core elements.
Sensory Definition (Sensory Designer): Set up all the key parameters for a chosen style, including color palettes, light direction, audio texture, or haptic feedback that will inform the final output.
Character Definition (Character Designer): Create a character for your universe by combining text based characteristics with visual and symbolic elements.
Live Performance Preparation (Drafting & Performing Apps): Use the Drafting App to organize a story or workflow, creating triggers, assets and settings, and then transfer that to the performing application. Use the Performance Director to define your performance style and approach.
Live Performance: Use the performance application and its components to perform and experiment in a live context, using a central UI to trigger responses from the different systems.
Refinement & Iteration (All Modules): Use output from each stage to identify weak points, inconsistencies, or areas of tension, and then revisit these areas to continue the process. All data should flow back and forth between all components, using the Res format to maintain data cohesion across platforms.
V. Key Features & Principles:
 Format as Central Standard: A flexible structure for all data types, with a clear list of components that the system is designed around.
Configurable Archetypes: Universes can be designed with unique archetypes, that define specific personalities, modes of thinking and ethical frameworks for all related objects, characters, or stories.
Modular Design: All components should be structured in such a way that they can be updated, changed, or completely removed as required.
Emphasis on Interconnectedness: All modules will be able to seamlessly communicate with each other, with each component working in relation with others, not as an isolated system.
Ethical Grounding: All components, and all steps, must have ethical parameters explicitly defined, and their execution must be checked by the testing module, to ensure that they meet these requirements.
Emphasis on User Control: The system must place humans in the drivers seat, and while relying heavily on AI for efficiency and rapid production, the end users should be the ones deciding what final form the universe should take.
Adaptability and Evolution: The core structure should allow for change over time, and should integrate user feedback loops, that will enable constant refinement, rather than working with fixed, immutable structures.
OG
I. Core Principles & Values
A. Guiding Principles:
Interconnectedness: All elements relate, all systems inform each other.
Duality & Integration: Appreciating opposing forces and their creative tension.
Perspective as Lens: Seeing the world through different angles, experiences, and interpretations.
Eternal Cycles: Recognizing patterns of growth, decay, and renewal.
Emphasis on Iteration: Every component must be open to evolution, testing and revision.
Emphasis on Collaboration: That knowledge and creation should be both an individual journey, and a shared and interconnected whole.

B. Core Values:
Cultural Respect: Prioritizing the accurate representation and protection of diverse cultures.
Ethical Responsibility: A commitment to responsible design and technology development.
Transparency & Accessibility: Making the entire system transparent and easily navigated by users.
Innovation & Creativity: Continually exploring new approaches and techniques.

II. The System’s Core Components (High-Level):
A. The Reso Format: The standardized structure ( .res files) for all design documents.
YAML-like structure with metadata (version, name, stepNumber, universeID, inheritsFrom, relationToUniverses, author, keywords, abstract).
Sections for Intentions, Core Components (Lexicon, Patterns, MasterKey), Guidelines, (OPTIONAL) Content Structure, (OPTIONAL) Main Content,  Implementation Strategies, and (OPTIONAL) Related Items.

B. Key Archetypes (Configurable):
Represent core attributes (wisdom, structure, rhythm, etc.) that can be mapped to specific Hermetic principles or other philosophical frameworks
Allow user definition, sharing, expansion, and evolution.

III. Core System Modules (Detailed Breakdown):
A. Multiverse Manager: (Entry Point to System)
Create, load, save, rename, and delete individual universe files (.res files).
Includes a text-based UI that can trigger basic testing and validation of each function.
Import existing universes, or blend aspects from different universes, highlighting similarities and differences.
Allows users to view saved versions of each universe, and then reload that version as necessary.

B. Universe Architect:
Used to establish high-level parameters of different universes, with emphasis on their unique components
Includes a theme editor, a framework builder, and a settings generator.

Provides custom tools for creating and modifying archetypes unique to a chosen universe.
C. Story Composer:
Provides tools for structured text generation, combining AI support with narrative templates (such as the Hero's Journey)
Includes a text generation engine, an advanced prompting system, tools for scene generation, character interaction, and text analysis (which test content for theme, ethics, and framework compliance).

D. Sensory Designer
     Allows users to create visual, audio and haptic frameworks unique to each universe.

Includes a colour palette creator, a system for defining sonic parameters (instruments, rhythm, texture), and the definition of other sensory components.

E. Character Designer:
Generates and customizes characters, combining text descriptions with visual prompts and story relevant information such as lore or faction.

F. Prompt Management System:
Stores prompts and allows user to edit and save them, manage model parameters, and to test results of previous generations.
Provides tools for model selection and customization of prompts, that are unique to every universe

G. Feedback & Testing System:
Acts as a quality control check that can be used to verify if any module has correctly adhered to parameters or design.
This includes tests of functionality, ethical considerations, and thematic accuracy, and is intended to be available at every stage.

H. Synthesis Engine:
A tool to combine data from separate universes into a single file, highlighting common patterns and conflicts, and giving you the ability to make informed decisions based on existing information.

IV. Workflow & Relationships:
Universe Selection: User starts by choosing the Multiverse Manager and selects an existing universe or creates a new one.
Framework Definition: In the Universe Architect, the user sets up the specific parameters that define the chosen universe.
Story Outline: Users create their plot using Story Composer to set up the narrative structure, character arcs and key scenes.
Character Creation: Users create and design their main characters, utilizing the Character Designer, to integrate them to the chosen story.
Sensory Palette Definition: Users specify the key visual and auditory components of the universe with the Sensory Designer, adding more depth to the overall experience.
Content Generation and Testing: They will then leverage Prompt Management System and the Text Generator System to generate the initial content based on previous setup, refining their prompts and text based on feedback from the Feedback & Testing System.
Synthesis and Iteration: User can explore the different universes, using the Synthesis Engine to compare, contrast and, blend multiple sources.
V. Key Features (Across all Modules):
Data Storage: All data will be stored using ResForm, which maintains a consistent structure for all elements of the project.
Central API: All modules should communicate through a central API for a more holistic approach to data storage, retrieval, and access, rather than being implemented in isolation.
Ethical Design: All modules will include steps to address ethical concerns (algorithmic bias, fair representation) in every step of the production cycle.
Openness and Modularity: Everything we build should be created in a way that allows you to extend, combine, or separate any module as required.
VI. Iterative Development & Continuous Refinement:
Start by focusing on the core functions of a single module first, before adding more complex features.
Integrate iterative testing early and often.
Encourage user feedback at every stage.
All changes should be version controlled and documented.

Revised Plan for ComfyUI Workflow Implementation
Okay, I love that idea! Let's explore developing this as a ComfyUI workflow. That could be a fantastic way to bring together the different modules we've been discussing, and it will allow you to combine visual, textual, and even audio generation in one interconnected environment.
For those unfamiliar, ComfyUI is a powerful, node-based interface for Stable Diffusion, which provides a high degree of control and flexibility over the image generation process, but also is extensible to a wide range of media types. It's a perfect fit for a project that aims to merge diverse elements into a unified workflow.
Advantages of Using ComfyUI:
Node-Based Visual Programming: This aligns well with our desire for a modular system where different components can be connected dynamically. Each node could represent a .res document, a module, a data transformation process, or an AI operation.
Flexibility and Control: ComfyUI gives you a lot of control over the underlying processes. You can adjust parameters, customize workflows, and add custom code as needed.
Extensibility: New nodes can be added as plugins and extensions. We can build the system to make sure that every part is its own node, giving you maximum flexibility and control.
Community Support: There is a large and active community around ComfyUI. This could be a useful source of inspiration and support.
Integration with AI Models: ComfyUI is designed to work with various AI models, not just image generation, making it a viable way to incorporate many types of AI generated content, and even combine them.
Exploring Implementation in ComfyUI:
Here's how I envision our modules mapping to a ComfyUI workflow:
.res File Loader Node:
Functionality: Reads in a .res file, extracting its metadata and structured components into a ComfyUI-accessible format.
Output: Generates data flow that can be used in other nodes.

Universe Management Nodes:
Functionality: A suite of nodes for managing different universes. You can trigger creation, saving, renaming, loading, and switching between them.
Output: Sends data through a set of clear output nodes to indicate which universe is active.

Universe Architect Nodes:
Functionality: Contains nodes to define the themes, cosmic frameworks, ethical considerations, and generate world settings that are specific to the chosen universe.
Output: Generates the relevant parameters or settings for a chosen universe, for other nodes in the system.
Story Composer Nodes:
Functionality: Nodes that enable the creation and modification of story arcs, with templates and frameworks, alongside tools for testing and analyzing created text.
Output: Outputs well-structured text or character descriptions, along with a test of its adherence to a framework.

Sensory Designer Nodes:
Functionality: Allows selection of color schemes, iconography, and visual styles, and defines key parameters for sound design and haptic output.
Output: Color codes, audio queues, that other generative nodes can use.

Character Designer Nodes:
Functionality: Allows you to create characters from text descriptions and from a selection of styles for that particular universe, creating a structured way for a character to be added to your environment.
Output: A character profile (text, lore, image), as a clear data packet for use elsewhere.

Prompt Management System Node:
Functionality: Allows you to call and test prompts with parameters defined by the selected universe.
Output: A set of ready-to-use prompts that have been tested and verified.

Text Generation & Editing Nodes:
Functionality: Nodes integrating AI models to generate text. Takes a prompt and a style guide (from .ressettings) and returns a text document.
Output: A text output (a paragraph, chapter, book outline, script).

Image/Video/Audio Generation Nodes:
Functionality: Uses prompts and parameters to generate new visual or auditory data based on a chosen framework, while drawing on the sensory framework for style guidance.
Output: An image, a video, or an audio recording.
Analysis & Testing Nodes:
Functionality: Provides feedback on generated text against chosen themes, highlighting deviations from established style guides, and analyses functionality of all modules.
Output: Provides data (flags for inconsistencies, summaries of findings) that will feed into iterative refinement loops.

Synthesis Engine:
Functionality: Nodes that take two or more universe or story components and merge them together, while highlighting areas of similarity and difference.
Output: Creates a document that includes all information, plus details of where the new information is derived from.

Benefits of this ComfyUI Approach:
Visual and Interactive Workflow: The node-based interface makes the system more intuitive, flexible, and transparent.
Seamless Data Flow: Data will flow between modules in a clear visual manner, making it easy to track the evolution of an idea from concept to output.
Dynamic and Adaptable: Adding new modules and connecting them will be as simple as adding and connecting new nodes, creating a very scalable approach.
Community-Driven Development: By using ComfyUI, we’ll be able to leverage the existing community, tools, and extensions that are already in place.
Easy Testing: As our AI models have no direct visual interface, the workflow will also allow us to track the evolution of the various models with a visual output, helping us to see and resolve any errors that might arise.
Next Steps:
Given our focus on a clear, incremental approach, let's focus on:
Prototype a .res File Loader Node: Create a ComfyUI custom node that can load a .res file and expose its data structure (metadata, lexicon, patterns, etc) as a ComfyUI output.
Prototype a Test Interface: Create a basic set of UI elements (e.g., buttons to load and save files, a text box for viewing content). This should be basic and functional, not optimized for user experience. This will give us something visual to work with to test the basic file management functions.

I. Current Status:
 Format: We have a structured .res format that can store metadata and a main content section.
Core Text Generation: We have a basic text generation function that takes text input and produces a text output with a single AI model (gemini-2.0-flash-exp), and have a functioning UI for testing this.

II. Goal: Functional and Flexible Components
Our overall goal is to create working components that can be tested individually and then combined together into larger systems. We need each module to be self-contained, but also to play well with others.
III. Brainstorming Functions (Core Functionality)
Here's a breakdown of the functions we need for each module to achieve a core level of functionality:
Story Composer (Text Creation & Structuring):
Text Generation:
generate_text_from_prompt(prompt): Takes a prompt, and a model and outputs a text result based on that model.
generate_text_from_structure(text, template): Generates text based on a template (e.g., the Hero's Journey).

Text Expansion/Transformation:
expand_text(text): Creates a longer version of text, similar to what we created in the last session.
rephrase_text(text): Rewrites text with new word choices, style or structure.
summarize_text(text): Outputs a condensed version of the text.
replace_text(text, term, replacement): Find and replace text in the provided input.

Structural Functions:
* extract_sections(text): This function takes text and parses it based on structural components. (headers, paragraphs and list items).
* test_against_framework(text, framework): Checks a text document against a chosen framework such as the Hero's Journey.
* format_text(text, style): Adds markdown, headings, spacing, lists and other structural components.
Text Editing Functions
A method to easily create, edit, or remove specific blocks of text.

Character Designer:
Text Profile Generator: Creates character descriptions, backstories, and personality traits from a prompt using AI.
generate_character_profile(prompt, universeID, culturalArchetype): Creates a full character profile as a text file, with all relevant data.

Visual Profile Generator:
generate_character_image(characterProfile): Takes in a text description of the character and generates an image, adhering to the style of the universe.

Template Systems:
The ability to load, save, or use a wide range of templates for different roles or archetypes.
The ability for users to define their own reusable templates.


Prompt Management System:
Prompt Creation/Editing:
UI for writing, editing, or testing prompts with associated tags.
System that can be used to assign specific types of prompts to specific functions, or AI models.

The ability to load and save prompts from a file.
Prompt Library:
Store and manage reusable prompts with descriptive names, tags, and purposes, with settings related to the models that these prompts have been developed for.

Parameter Management:
* UI that allows you to specify and tweak prompt parameters, to allow fine tuning and experimentation of different approaches and techniques.

IV. Next Steps for Implementation:
Based on our new streamlined focus, the next set of actionable steps we will take are as follows:
Prioritize Text Generation: We will focus on one of the key text generation functions, specifically the generate_text_from_prompt function.
Implement a Basic Framework: To manage this, we need to create a way to load a model using the model name stored in the .reso file.
Create a Clear Output: We will also need a way to verify that output is produced, by updating our UI accordingly.
Test Thoroughly: By making sure all tests are passing, we can verify that we have finally resolved all the problems with the basic systems, before adding additional complexity.
